docs.title: Motor Power Control System
docs.text:
1. H-Bridge PWM

    • $0.89/each
    • Amazon Link H-Bridge
    Pros Cons Inexpensive Heat Can be run with PWM Motor wear

  2. Low Pass Filter PWM with H-Bridge

    • $0.99/each
    • Amazon Link H-Bridge
    Pros Cons Cheap Heat Changes PWM to constant lower voltage Higher power drain for battery

  3. MOSFET

    • $0.99/each
    • Amazon MOSFET
    Pros Cons Simple Unidirectional Cheap No brake for motor

Choice: Option 2: Low Pass Filter PWM with H-Bridge

Rationale: The low pass filter with an h-bridge is simple to implement while also being cost effective and meeting all the requirements for controlling the motor speed and precision. While it does suffer from the greater heat and wasted power it does not put extra wear on the motor like just PWM with an h-bridge and it can fully control the motor unlike only a single MOSFET.

docs.title: LED Error Code System
docs.text:
1. Single RGB LED

    • $0.09/each
    • Amazon RGB LED
    Pros Cons Simple Potential issues for colorblind users Easy to implement with each color representing an error Additional wiring

  2. 3 Single Color LEDs

    • $0.18/set of 3
    • Amazon LED
    Pros Cons Many possible states with on, off, or flashing Additional wiring and pins used Clear to user More space

  3. Single Flashing LED

    • $0.06/each
    • Amazon LED
    Pros Cons Simplest design Harder to tell specific codes with flashes Cheapest

Choice: Option 2: 3 Single Color LEDs

Rationale: The 3 single color LEDs are simple to implement and have 27 different possible combinations. The 3 LEDs are the most expensive and use the most pins on the microcontroller, but despite this, the additional information provided to the user will be far more valuable than the potential lost uses for those pins and space.

docs.title: Watchdog Timer
docs.text:
1. Internal Watchdog Timer

    • No cost already on Curiosity Nano
    Pros Cons Simple Vulnerable to system wide failure Cheap Potential debugging issues

  2. External Watchdog Timer

    • $1.77/each
    • Digikey Watchdog Timer
    Pros Cons Independent from microcontroller More expensive Hardware shutdown capability Additional board space

  3. Windowed Watchdog Timer

    • Already on Curiosity Nano
    Pros Cons Strict timing Higher complexity Catches loops Possible debugging issues

Choice: Option 3: Windowed Watchdog Timer

Rationale: The windowed watchdog timer will not take up additional board space and will allow for more accurate catching of issues. Despite the higher software complexity the additional functionality will help users to detect issues before they cause permanent problems.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This schematic is design to support control of a motor through an H bridge being controlled by a PWM signal from a microcontroller. It uses an LC filter to minimize wear from PWM control by using an analog Voltage.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: I used the datasheets for the parts I used as well as the standard amperage for a 12V DC motor for the H-bridge[cite: 5]. I used this data to determine what voltage regulator to use for the Curiosity Nano and came to the conclusion to use the LM7805 voltage regulator[cite: 5]. I did a power budget because it is important to understand the amount of power used by a system to determine the lifetime it will have when on battery power and the impact it will have on the electrical system if it is plugged in for power.

docs.title: Conclusions
docs.text: From the prepared Power Budget, I believe that the lifespan of a battery running a single motor controller and motor will be more than enough for most uses even at maximum power usage. Even though some power will be lost to heat through the H-bridge it is still efficient enough to run for several hours at maximum load.
